agentEngineering.title: How I work with AI coding agents
agentEngineering.intro: I have switched my monthly subscription to whichever model did the work best at the time. I used Claude Code at work from its early versions, moved to Codex after GPT-5.3, and now mainly use Opus 5.5 with Claude Code. Each time I switched tools I reviewed the existing skills and settings and deleted rules that were no longer needed.

results.travelRecords: I built Travel Records with Claude Code and keep its working rules and context in CLAUDE.md, so adding a new trip is a repeatable flow.
results.devtoolCli: react-devtool-cli is a CLI that lets agents inspect React apps without the browser DevTools, and it ships skills for Codex, Claude Code, and Gemini CLI.
results.verification: This portfolio and POCAZ keep agent rules in AGENTS.md, and a change counts as done only after lint, tests, and the build pass.

agentEngineering.verificationDescription: Code an agent changed has to pass this command too.

AboutPage.title: About Me
AboutPage.intro: I'm a frontend developer with four years of professional experience. At ScatterX I spent three years building the frontend of a B2B data analysis and visualization SaaS, and on the move of a jQuery analytics platform to Next.js I handled the initial setup, the UI core, and the architecture. Before that I built the frontend of an accounting service for hospitals at SUGARBRICKS and worked on ERP development at sysware. I build and run my personal projects on my own, from planning through the server and deployment.

AboutPage.name: Manjoong Kim

scatterx.summary: A B2B data analysis and visualization SaaS used by manufacturing affiliates of large Korean companies (XMORSE, SaharaX)
highlights: With one teammate, I moved a jQuery analytics platform to Next.js over one year and five months, producing XMORSE 2.0. I handled the initial setup, the UI core, and the architecture.
Request and response types are generated automatically from the backend OpenAPI spec, so a spec change shows up at build time.
I moved the chart iframe screen embedded in other services from SSR to SSG, bringing first load under 0.5 seconds, and changed host communication to a handshake.
I wrote unit tests, React Testing Library tests, and Playwright E2E tests myself, and reviewed PRs against the team conventions.
In early development of the new product SaharaX, I built most of the UI except the editor core with Web Components and no framework.
I built the frontend of an accounting service for hospitals.
